text: The sky turned rosy pink at close of day.
Sunny watched the colours softly fade.
Down from the clouds there fluttered something bright,
pink and grey and chattering with joy.
A galah! With feathers pink as fairy floss,
and a cheeky little crest upon her head.
“Hello!” she squawked. “I'm heading home to roost!
The whole sky's going pink — that means it's bedtime!”
“The sky is pink like you,” said Sunny, smiling.
“It borrowed my best colour,” laughed the bird.
She hopped along the branch from foot to foot,
one last little dance before her sleep.
Then all her flock came wheeling softly home,
a hundred rosy wings against the dusk.
They settled in the old gum tree together,
murmuring soft goodnights from branch to branch.
The little galah fluffed up soft and round,
and tucked her head beneath her rosy wing.
The chattering hushed. The tree grew still and calm,
all full of sleeping birds like soft pink flowers.
Sunny found her spot beneath the tree,
and curled up as the last pink left the sky.
The night came velvet-blue and full of stars.
Everything was peaceful, soft, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy under sleeping birds.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beneath the roosting tree,
dreaming in the softest shade of pink.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, pink galah.
Goodnight, sleepy flock. Goodnight, little one.
